title: Two-Basin routed surface system with shared groundwater redistribution

dependency_gate.implementation_rule: No DUMMY-17 model or tests before DUMMY-16 closes and the implementation baseline is rebound.

purpose: Introduce the minimum spatial topology in which water can move from an upstream Basin to a downstream Basin simultaneously through explicit surface routing and through a shared groundwater store, while every path remains analytically separable and exactly conservative.

first_stage_boundary.reason: Qualify the physical network ledger and path decomposition before management allocation is reintroduced.

equations.total: d(A h_1 + A h_2 + A_g h_g)/dt = 0

mode_decomposition.interpretation: Surface routing affects the inter-Basin difference mode but cancels from the common surface-groundwater mode; shared groundwater exchange affects both modes through C.

canonical_case.interpretation: At t=0 the downstream Basin receives 20 m3/time directly by surface routing and 20 m3/time indirectly by groundwater drainage, while the upstream Basin simultaneously infiltrates 30 m3/time to groundwater.

hypotheses: The canonical total storage remains exactly 140 m3 for all finite time.
The surface-routing flux appears with opposite signs in the two Basin ledgers and cancels from Basin1+Basin2+groundwater total storage.
Each Basin-groundwater exchange appears once in its Basin ledger and with opposite sign in the shared groundwater ledger.
At t=0 Basin2 receives equal 20 m3/time contributions from direct surface routing and groundwater drainage, demonstrating two simultaneous internal pathways from the upstream/shared system.
The inter-Basin head-difference mode decays as exp(-0.9 t), independently of the common weighted storage mode.
The surface-mean/groundwater contrast decays as 0.1 exp(-1.5 t), independently of the routing conductance K_r except through the difference mode.

A model can conserve total water while misassigning water between the direct surface route and the groundwater-mediated pathway; path/transfer ownership therefore needs separate qualification from total conservation.
